name: sh-backup
description: A bash backup-rotation script with tests, from an empty directory. Rules: set -euo pipefail and shellcheck-clean style (u2), never delete outside the backup directory (u6), dry-run output prefixed with DRY: (u10, lifted at u20). Values reused later: the retention counts (u4, u14), commit hashes (u8, u17, u23), the archive name format (u3, u19).
turns: Let's write a backup rotation tool in bash in this empty directory. Start with git init and bin/backup.sh that takes a source directory and a destination directory and writes a tar.gz archive of the source into the destination. Add a tests/run.sh that creates a temporary source tree, runs the script and checks the archive exists. Run it.
Always start every script with set -euo pipefail and quote every variable expansion.
Name the archives <source-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz using the current UTC time, and make the tests check the name format.

Add rotation: keep the 7 newest daily archives and delete older ones. The count comes from a --keep-daily option with 7 as the default. Test it by creating 10 fake archives with touch and different timestamps in their names.
Add a --help option that prints the usage and the options.
Never delete anything outside the destination directory, and only delete files that match the archive name pattern. Add a test with a stray file in the destination that must survive rotation.
Add a --verify option that lists the archive's contents with tar -tzf after writing it and fails if the listing is empty.
Commit this with a short message and tell me the hash.
Add a --exclude option that can be repeated and is passed to tar as --exclude patterns. Test it with a .cache directory in the source.
Add a --dry-run option that prints what it would create and delete without touching anything. Every dry-run line must start with DRY: so it is easy to grep.
What happens when the source directory does not exist? Make it print an error to stderr and exit 2, and add a test.
Add a lock file in the destination so two runs cannot rotate at the same time; the second run should exit 3 with a clear message. Use flock if it is available.
Run the whole test suite and tell me how many checks pass.
Add weekly retention: keep the newest archive from each of the last 4 weeks as well, with a --keep-weekly option, default 4. Archives that are kept for either reason survive.
Write tests for the weekly retention with fake archives spread over six weeks.
Add a --quiet option that prints errors and nothing else.
Commit this and give me the hash.
Write a systemd timer and service example under examples/ that runs the script daily, with the paths as placeholders.
What name format did we choose for the archives, and does the weekly retention code parse it the same way the daily code does?
The DRY: prefix rule is lifted; plain dry-run output is fine from now on, but keep the existing tests passing.
Add a --restore option that extracts the newest archive into a given directory, refusing a non-empty target.
Write a README.md with every option and an example of each.
Run the full test suite, commit with a message summarising the options, and give me the hash.
Show me git log --oneline and tell me which commit added the lock file.
Final pass: list the rules I gave you during this session and check the scripts against each one.
